title: ROS 2: The Robotic Nervous System Quiz

questions.explanation: ROS stands for Robot Operating System. It's a flexible framework for writing robot software as a collection of tools and libraries.

questions.text: In ROS 2, what is a Node?
options: A process that performs computation and communicates with other nodes
A data storage unit in the network
A configuration file for robot behavior
questions.explanation: A Node is a process that executes computation. Nodes communicate with each other via Topics and Services to form a complete robot control system.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between Topics and Services in ROS 2?
options: Topics use pub/sub (one-way streaming), Services use request/response (synchronous)
Services are only for real-time systems
Topics can only transmit small messages
questions.explanation: Topics implement a publish/subscribe pattern for continuous data streaming, while Services implement a request/response pattern for discrete operations. Services are synchronous while Topics are asynchronous.

questions.text: ROS 2 is backwards compatible with ROS 1 code without any modifications.
questions.explanation: ROS 2 introduced significant architectural changes and is not backwards compatible with ROS 1. Code must be migrated to use ROS 2 APIs.

questions.text: What does rclpy stand for in ROS 2?
questions.explanation: rclpy is the Robot Client Library for Python. It provides the Python API for creating ROS 2 nodes, publishers, subscribers, and services.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a key component of a URDF file for describing a robot?
questions.explanation: URDF files describe the kinematic and dynamic structure of robots using links and joints. Motor manufacturer specifications are external documentation, not part of the URDF format.

questions.text: In a humanoid robot URDF, how would you represent the connection between the torso and an arm?
options: As a joint connecting the torso link to the arm link
As a separate node in the network
As a service call between components
questions.explanation: The connection between body parts in a URDF is represented as a joint. A joint connects two links and defines the type of motion allowed (revolute, prismatic, fixed, etc.).

questions.text: In ROS 2, a Publisher node must know the identity of specific Subscriber nodes to send data.
questions.explanation: One advantage of the pub/sub pattern is loose coupling. Publishers don't need to know who subscribes to their topics - they just publish data, and any interested subscribers receive it.

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of using ROS 2 for humanoid robot control instead of custom code?
options: It guarantees the robot will never fail
It provides a standardized framework for communication, reusable libraries, and community support
It automatically generates optimal robot movements
It eliminates the need for simulation
questions.explanation: ROS 2 provides a comprehensive ecosystem with standardized communication protocols, well-tested libraries for common tasks, extensive documentation, and a large community. This accelerates development and improves reliability.

questions.text: URDF files can directly specify the control parameters (PID gains) for joint motors in a humanoid robot.
questions.explanation: URDF files only describe the structural and kinematic properties of robots. Control parameters like PID gains are specified separately in configuration files or controller definitions, not in the URDF.
